title: Heat @ Hawks — Official scorer wrongly fouls out Shaquille O'Neal; protest upheld, final 51.9s replayed, Hawks win 114-111 (Dec 19, 2007 - Mar 8, 2008)
incident_summary: The Hawks' official scoring table mistakenly credited a fourth-quarter foul (called on Udonis Haslem with 3:24 left in regulation) to Shaquille O'Neal. As a result, when O'Neal was whistled in overtime with the Hawks leading 112-111, the table ruled it his sixth foul and disqualified him — it was only his fifth. Al Horford's subsequent free throws made it 114-111. Miami protested; on Jan 11, 2008 the NBA upheld the protest (the first granted since December 1982), fined Atlanta $50,000 for 'grossly negligent' failure to follow scoring procedures, and ordered the final 51.9 seconds replayed before the teams' next meeting on March 8, 2008. Neither team scored in the replay; the official final became Hawks 114, Heat 111 in overtime (replacing the original 117-111 result).

sources_disagreed: Official scorer's book (foul on O'Neal) vs. on-court officiating/stat crew (foul on Haslem) — the stat crew noticed the mistake but the table failed to respond effectively

cause.detail: Confirmed scorer-table error: a Haslem foul was entered under O'Neal's name; the league-mandated timeout coordination between the official scorer and stat crew did not happen, so the mistake survived until after the game (when revised boxes showed O'Neal with six). Commissioner Stern ruled Atlanta 'grossly negligent' and fined the team $50,000.
